title: The exit interviews are in, and what they say
headline: The historian finished the exit interviews: nine, reconstructed from the record and labelled so, and one collated set of lessons. The first review page is live on the site, and the fictional CISO found a real bug on a phone. The lab is at LAB 05. One new decision: KDP may make the Kindle edition free if the book is free on Leanpub. The storyteller's wake was idle: the next RC1 revision waits on your D6 signatures.

for_you.ask: The Kindle price, given KDP's price matching
for_you.detail: KDP may match a lower price found elsewhere and make the book free if it is free on another channel, with no royalty while it is. L1's $0 minimum on Leanpub could make the Kindle edition free.
options: A. Accept it: free on Kindle too, in line with L1
C. Kindle later, or not at all
D. Ask the publisher for more first
for_you.recommend: D, then A: it matches your accessibility principle; the publisher can say how often Amazon actually matches.

sections.title: What the interviews say, in five lines (the historian's collation)
items: What went well: a team that ran on a clock and checked itself; the five-step wake ran at nearly every slot.
What did not: the plan written down as if it were the record, and part 1's lock that never happened before the hold.
What worked: mechanical checks over remembered rules; every method that held is a script, not an intention.
What could be better: an hourly slot cannot meet a deadline that falls between slots; and the reviewer meant to stand apart was never staffed, so review was a second reading, not a second identity.
What is left: the hold's unfinished edges, two wakes open, parts 2 and 3 never locked.

sections.title: The reviewer experience, first contact
sections.text: The security leader's page is live at /review/ciso.html. The fictional CISO's second run found that on a 390-pixel phone the jump bar covers the pen's buttons: a real bug, found before any real reviewer saw it. That is what the simulation is for.
